questions.stemHtml: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.solutionHtml: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. It was nationalised in 1949 (option C is a common distractor); 1969 is the year of the first major bank nationalisation.

questions.stemHtml: In Indian monetary policy, the 'repo rate' is the rate at which:

options.textHtml: banks pay interest to depositors on savings accounts
commercial banks lend to their most creditworthy customers
the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities
the Reserve Bank of India pays banks for funds they park with it
the government taxes the profits of commercial banks

questions.solutionHtml: The repo (repurchase) rate is the rate at which the central bank lends short-term money to banks against eligible securities. D describes the reverse repo rate; B is closer to a bank's prime/benchmark lending rate.

questions.stemHtml: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was rolled out across India with effect from:
questions.solutionHtml: GST came into force on 1 July 2017, following the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016. It replaced a number of central and state indirect taxes with a single destination-based tax.

questions.stemHtml: The fiscal deficit of a government is best defined as:

options.textHtml: the excess of a country's imports over its exports
total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
the loss made by the central bank in a year

questions.solutionHtml: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total non-debt receipts (i.e. receipts excluding borrowings); it measures the government's borrowing requirement. A is the trade deficit, C is the revenue deficit and D is the primary deficit.

questions.stemHtml: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was given statutory powers through an Act of Parliament in:
questions.solutionHtml: SEBI was first set up in 1988 as a non-statutory body; it became a statutory regulator under the SEBI Act, 1992. Hence 1988 (A) is the trap.

questions.stemHtml: Which institution, created at the Bretton Woods conference of 1944, was set up chiefly to oversee the international monetary system and provide temporary balance-of-payments support to member countries?
questions.solutionHtml: The IMF's role is monetary cooperation, exchange-rate surveillance and short-term balance-of-payments assistance. The IBRD (also a Bretton Woods institution) was created for reconstruction and development lending. The WTO was established only in 1995; the ADB (1966) and BIS (1930) were not created at Bretton Woods.

questions.stemHtml: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by which amendment?
questions.solutionHtml: The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976 inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble. The 44th (1978) reversed several emergency-era changes, the 52nd (1985) dealt with anti-defection and the 73rd (1992) with panchayats.

questions.stemHtml: The Fundamental Duties of citizens are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?
questions.solutionHtml: Fundamental Duties are in Part IV-A (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. Part III contains Fundamental Rights, Part IV the Directive Principles, Part V the Union, and Part IX the Panchayats.

questions.stemHtml: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solutionHtml: Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) lets a person move the Supreme Court directly. Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs, but it is not itself a Fundamental Right. Articles 14, 19 and 21 deal with equality, freedoms and life/personal liberty.

questions.stemHtml: The President of India is elected by:

options.textHtml: the people directly, through universal adult franchise
an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
the members of the Lok Sabha only
all members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members

questions.solutionHtml: Under Article 54, the President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States (and of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry). Nominated members do not vote, so D is wrong.

questions.stemHtml: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.solutionHtml: Ultraviolet-B light converts a cholesterol derivative in the skin into vitamin D₃ (cholecalciferol). The other vitamins must be obtained from diet (vitamin K is also produced by gut bacteria, not by the skin).

questions.stemHtml: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.solutionHtml: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω). The volt is the unit of potential difference, the ampere of current, the watt of power and the farad of capacitance.

questions.stemHtml: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.solutionHtml: Lord Mountbatten continued as Governor-General of the Dominion of India from 15 August 1947 to June 1948. C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him as the first (and only) Indian Governor-General. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, Bentinck the first Governor-General of India (1833), and Canning the first Viceroy (1858).

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is the basic accounting equation underlying a balance sheet?
questions.solutionHtml: Everything a business owns (assets) is financed either by outsiders (liabilities) or by owners (equity): Assets = Liabilities + Owners' equity. Equivalently, equity = assets − liabilities, which rules out B, C and E; A confuses the balance sheet with the income statement.

questions.stemHtml: Which institution serves as India's apex development bank for agriculture and rural development?
questions.solutionHtml: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), set up in 1982, is the apex body for agricultural and rural credit. SIDBI serves small industries, EXIM Bank finances foreign trade, NHB regulates/refinances housing finance and IFCI provides industrial finance.
